flashcard_questions.q: How many bars long is Chorus 1 of Africa?
Which chord pattern is used for the first three phrases of the chorus?
How many different pitches does the chorus melody use in its first three phrases?
flashcard_questions.a: Only two — the tonic A and the leading note G#.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the vocal texture change through Chorus 1?
flashcard_questions.a: It builds from a solo voice to a duet and then to three parts.

flashcard_questions.q: Which chord replaces chord V in the fourth bar of the chorus's final phrase?
What is the job of the link sections in Africa?
flashcard_questions.a: To move from the A major chorus back to B major.

flashcard_questions.q: How many times is Riff a stated in each link section?
How many bars long is Verse 2 of Africa?
Why is Verse 2 shorter than Verse 1?
flashcard_questions.a: The 9-bar phrase goes round twice instead of three times.

flashcard_questions.q: Which new melodic line is heard above the texture in Verse 2?
flashcard_questions.a: A flute-like countermelody, also called a descant.

flashcard_questions.q: Where in Verse 2 does the melody leap higher than in Verse 1?
flashcard_questions.a: In bar 33, up to the pitches D# and C#.

flashcard_questions.q: How many bars long is the instrumental section of Africa?
Which riff is developed in the instrumental section of Africa?

flashcard_questions.a: A group of notes sung to a single syllable of text.
The rate at which the chords change in a piece of music.

notes: 15 cards: 5 chorus cards (length, chord pattern, two-pitch melody, texture build, substituted chord iii), 3 link/verse-2 cards, 3 instrumental cards, 1 cause card (why Verse 2 is shorter) and 2 term-to-definition cards (melisma, harmonic rhythm). Section names used throughout instead of lyrics. Dropped tonic, leading note, pentatonic and grace notes as glossary terms already tested elsewhere in the unit or too minor to earn a card.
